To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the small x behavior of the proton structure functions, as measured in deep inelastic lepton-proton collisions, can be understood in the context of perturbative quantum chromodynamics, and that the small x gluon distribution in the proton is very small.

The cross sections for Z and W production at the LHC and SSC are significantly larger than previously calculated, and that this enhancement is a consequence of a new component in the cross sections at large rapidity which arises when the gluon distribution contains a component with extremely small χ.

The cross sections for Z production at hadronic colliders depend on the gluon density at small x and that a gluon density with χ − 4 behaviour at small x gives a good description of the data at LHC energies.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there are no compelling reasons to believe that the gluon distributions at small χ are very different from those at larger χ.
there is a small but non-negligible effect on the W, Z cross sections due to very small χ parton distributions.
the small χ behaviour of the gluon density is not yet established, and that a number of models are consistent with the data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the small χ behaviour of the gluon is not yet well determined and that a measurement of W, Z production at large rapidity would be a useful test.
the small χ gluon component in the parton distributions of most models is not consistent with the data.
the small χ behaviour of the gluon is a crucial ingredient in the description of high energy hadron colliders.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the W and Z cross sections at the LHC are sensitive to the behaviour of the gluon distribution at extremely small χ.
the small χ component is not only large, but also very distinctive, in that it has a different energy and rapidity dependence from the rest of the cross section.
W and Z production can provide a probe of small-χ partons.
